collection.search_terms: diodorus siculus bibliotheca library of history egypt osiris isis hermes thoth gods kings first men nile colonies hecataeus
collection.description: Diodorus of Sicily's account of the Egyptian traditions on the first men, the gods who ruled Egypt as kings, the deeds and death of Osiris, the colonies said to have gone out from Egypt, and the 18,000 years of gods and heroes, on the pages of the 10th-century Vatican manuscript.

texts.title: Diodorus Siculus 1.10-13: the first men, the eternal gods and the god-kings of Egypt
texts.source: Vat. gr. 130 (10th c.) via DigiVatLib IIIF + Vogel Greek (Perseus, checked against the 1888 printing) + Oldfather English (Loeb 1933, public domain)
texts.description: The Egyptian account in Diodorus of how the first men came into being in Egypt from the mud of the Nile, of the sun and moon as the eternal gods Osiris and Isis, of the elements as gods, and of the earthly gods who ruled Egypt as kings, from Helius or Hephaestus to Cronus and Osiris.

texts.title: Diodorus Siculus 1.14-16: Isis and Osiris as givers of grain, wine and law; Hermes the inventor
texts.source: Vat. gr. 130 (10th c.) via DigiVatLib IIIF + Vogel Greek (Perseus, checked against the 1888 printing) + Oldfather English (Loeb 1933, public domain)
texts.description: Isis discovers wheat and barley and gives laws, Osiris founds Thebes and teaches the vine, and Hermes invents letters, music, astronomy and the olive, in Diodorus' account of the Egyptian gods who ruled as kings.

texts.title: Diodorus Siculus 1.17-20: the campaign of Osiris through the inhabited world
texts.source: Vat. gr. 130 (10th c.) via DigiVatLib IIIF + Vogel Greek (Perseus, checked against the 1888 printing) + Oldfather English (Loeb 1933, public domain)
texts.description: Osiris leaves Isis to rule Egypt and travels with Anubis, Macedon, Pan, the Muses and the Satyrs through Ethiopia, Arabia and India to Thrace, teaching agriculture and the vine, while Heracles stops the flood of the Nile.

texts.title: Diodorus Siculus 1.21-22: the death of Osiris, the vengeance of Isis and the tombs of the gods
texts.source: Vat. gr. 130 (10th c.) via DigiVatLib IIIF + Vogel Greek (Perseus, checked against the 1888 printing) + Oldfather English (Loeb 1933, public domain)
texts.description: Typhon murders Osiris and divides his body into twenty-six pieces; Isis and Horus avenge him, Isis gives each order of priests a share of the burial, and the tombs of Isis and Osiris are shown at Memphis and at Philae.

texts.title: Diodorus Siculus 1.23-29: the age of the gods, the Egyptian Heracles, Isis the healer, the stelae of Isis and Osiris, and the colonies from Egypt
texts.source: Vat. gr. 130 (10th c.) via DigiVatLib IIIF + Vogel Greek (Perseus, checked against the 1888 printing) + Oldfather English (Loeb 1933, public domain)
texts.description: The Egyptian claims in Diodorus: more than ten thousand years from Osiris to Alexander, the gods' reigns of 1,200 and 300 years explained as lunar years, the giants, the inscriptions on the stelae of Isis and Osiris, and the colonies said to have gone out from Egypt to Babylon, Argos, Colchis, Judea and Athens.

texts.title: Diodorus Siculus 1.44: gods and heroes for almost 18,000 years, then mortal kings
texts.source: Vat. gr. 130 (10th c.) via DigiVatLib IIIF + Vogel Greek (Perseus, checked against the 1888 printing) + Oldfather English (Loeb 1933, public domain)
texts.description: Diodorus' summary of the Egyptian priests' chronology: gods and heroes ruled Egypt for a little less than 18,000 years, the last of them Horus son of Isis, and mortal kings for almost 5,000 years, 470 men and 5 women of native birth besides the Ethiopian, Persian and Macedonian rulers.
